mechanics.name: Autodidact
mechanics.currentEffect: While healing another Survivor without a Med-Kit, successful Healing Skill Checks grant 1 Token up to 3/4/5. Great Skill Checks cannot occur. Each Token improves Skill Check progression by 15 percentage points, starting at a 15% penalty with zero Tokens (then 0%, +15%, +30%, +45%, +60% as applicable).
activation: Heal another Survivor without a Med-Kit.
Complete a Healing Skill Check to gain a Token.
Ends/deactivates when: Does not activate while healing with a Med-Kit.
mechanics.patchNote: Latest live balance change (8.1.0): Reduced the initial Healing Skill Check progression penalty to -15%.
mechanics.plainEnglishSummary: Healing Skill Checks build tokens that improve later check progress, while Great Skill Checks are suppressed.
mechanics.tokenOrStackBehavior: Gain 1 Token per successful Healing Skill Check; tier caps are 3/4/5; Tokens persist for the Trial.
specialInteractions: Great Healing Skill Checks are suppressed.

editorial.summary: Healing Skill Checks build Tokens that turn later Good checks into enormous healing bursts, eventually reaching +60% progression at five Tokens.
useCases: Turn repeated teammate heals into increasingly explosive healing Skill Checks.
Recover a heavily injured team quickly once several Tokens have been earned.
Pair with effects that increase healing Skill Check frequency to reach the high-token state sooner.
counters: The first Skill Check starts with a 15% progression penalty.
Token gain depends on actually receiving healing Skill Checks.
The perk is inactive when healing with a Med-Kit.
pros: Very high healing ceiling at maximum Tokens.
Tokens persist and reward continued support play through the Trial.
Late-game Skill Checks can remove huge chunks of a heal instantly.
cons: Unreliable early game and vulnerable to poor Skill Check RNG.
Initial penalty can actively slow the first heals.
Requires repeated teammate healing to reach its best state.
analysis: Autodidact takes this position because few healing perks have such a dramatic gap between their opening and fully stacked states. At zero Tokens, a Skill Check actually loses 15% healing progress. At five Tokens, a successful check grants an enormous +60%, allowing one proc to erase most of the remaining heal.

The challenge is getting there. Tokens only arrive when healing Skill Checks occur, and the game does not promise them on demand. A fast early heal may complete before the perk generates meaningful stacks, leaving Autodidact worse than an empty perk slot for that interaction.

Once several Tokens are banked, the equation changes. Multi-injury situations become much easier to stabilize, and Empathy helps the user actively seek injured teammates to create more opportunities. One-Two-Three-Four! can also increase Skill Check frequency, making the stack-building phase less dependent on luck.

Autodidact sits in B rather than A because the first half of its progression is too inconsistent. A perk whose ceiling can be spectacular but whose floor can literally subtract healing progress needs that volatility reflected in the ranking.
editorial.verdict: A volatile healing engine that starts badly and can end brilliantly. Autodidact rewards dedicated support play, but Skill Check RNG prevents it from being a dependable top-tier option.
